model.description: Model is the Claude model that explains the report (default claude-opus-5).

AIConfig.description: AIConfig configures `den doctor --explain`, the only place den calls a language model — and only when asked, after showing what it would send.

auto_reveal.description: show every value in clear when opened

AWSSecretsManagerSecretSpec.description: AWSSecretsManagerSecretSpec is one AWS Secrets Manager secret, read with the SDK as aws_profile.

AWSSessionSpec.description: AWSSessionSpec curates one [sso-session ...] discovered in the AWS config.

sessions.description:
Sessions curates which discovered SSO sessions den shows, and in what
order. Empty means show every session found in the AWS config.

name.description:
Name is what the pop-up shows and what runbooks.agent and `den runbook
new --agent` refer to.

command.description:
Command is the command line, split on whitespace (no shell quoting):
`claude --model opus`, `ollama launch claude --model glm-5:cloud`.
den adds its own arguments after it.

kind.description:
Kind says which agent CLI the command starts, so den passes the
arguments that CLI takes: claude (Claude Code), codex (Codex), opencode
(OpenCode), copilot (Copilot CLI), qwen (Qwen Code), droid (Droid), pi
(Pi) or kimi (Kimi Code). Empty infers it from a command starting with
one of them, or `ollama launch <kind>` (copilot-cli for copilot); any
other wrapper needs it.

AgentSpec.description: AgentSpec is one named way to start an agent that writes a runbook.

compose_file.description: the Compose file, relative to where den runs or absolute

services.description: the Compose services to start; every one when empty

region.description: a label you choose, e.g. eu or us; shown to people and runbooks, den does not interpret it

environment.description: a label you choose, e.g. dev, staging or prod; prod and production count as production

production.description: an agent connects a production service only if mcp.allow_production is set, and then asks the user; implied by environment: prod

local_port.description: local end of the tunnel; each type has its own default (RDS 50432, Redshift 55439, Redis 16379, DocumentDB 27017, OpenSearch 59200, Neptune 58182)

reconnect.description: auto-reopen the SSM port-forward if it drops (e.g. SSM idle timeout); the IAM token is renewed while connected either way

ec2_instance_id.description: the bastion instance the SSM transport forwards through

aws_profile.description: profile the SSM session runs as

credential_profile.description: profile credentials are minted as, and the identity the data store sees; aws_profile when unset

aws_region_code.description: AWS region of the bastion and of the credential calls

transport.description: how the network is reached; SSM when unset

db_name.description: optional, placed in the URI path

KeePassXCSecretSpec.description: KeePassXCSecretSpec is one entry of a KeePass database, read with keepassxc-cli.

LogsConfig.description: LogsConfig controls file-based logging and log level filtering.

allow.description:
Allow lists the services agents may see, by name, with * and ?
wildcards; empty means all of them.

allow_production.description:
AllowProduction lets agents connect production services — and even then
only after the user confirms each connect in their MCP client.

allow_runbooks.description:
AllowRunbooks lets agents list and run runbooks; a runbook marked
confirm: true still asks the user first.

allow_source_runbooks.description:
AllowSourceRunbooks also lets agents list and run the runbooks of
runbooks.sources, and even then each run asks the user first.

MCPConfig.description: MCPConfig limits what an AI agent may do through `den mcp`.

update_pgpass.description: keep ~/.pgpass in sync with the current credential

db_user.description:
DBUser is provisioned-only: set, den calls GetClusterCredentials for that
user; unset, GetClusterCredentialsWithIAM maps the caller's IAM identity.

until_success.description: run again until the exit code is 0; needs max_attempts or timeout

RetrySpec.description: RetrySpec re-runs a runbook until it exits 0.

history.description:
History is how many finished runs are kept on disk; 0 keeps only the
last run, in memory. Default 20.

about.description:
About shows the About tab: the folder's README.md, the environment den
sets and the parameters. Default true.

shell.description:
Shell is the command t opens in the runbook's folder, e.g.
"bash --rcfile .venv/bin/activate". Default $SHELL.

editor.description:
Editor is the command e opens the runbook's script with, and o a run's
log. Default $VISUAL, then $EDITOR, then vi.

agent.description:
Agent is the agent E changes the runbook with: a command line such as
`claude --model opus`, the name of a runbooks.agents entry, a kind such
as claude or opencode, or auto. Default runbooks.agent.

RunbookSettings.description: RunbookSettings are how den presents a runbook rather than what it runs.

name.description:
Name prefixes the names of its runbooks: lower case letters, digits
and dashes.

url.description:
URL is the repository: https://host/owner/repo,
git@host:owner/repo.git, host/owner/repo, or owner/repo on GitHub.
Credentials come from git (a credential helper or an SSH key), never
from the URL.

ref.description:
Ref is the tag, branch or commit to check out; empty is the
repository's default branch. A tag or a commit stays put; a branch
moves on `den runbook source update`.

path.description:
Path is the folder of the repository holding the runbook folders;
empty is its root.

include.description:
Include lists the runbook folders to show, with * wildcards; empty
shows every one. `den runbook install` and `uninstall` edit it.

exclude.description: Exclude hides runbook folders Include would show.

env_map.description:
EnvMap maps the env names the source's runbooks use to entries of
environments. A runbook whose env is not mapped is not shown: its
author's "prod" is not necessarily yours.

RunbookSource.description: RunbookSource is a git repository of runbook folders.

name.description: what the Runbooks list shows and sequences refer to

cwd.description: working directory; relative to den.yaml's directory

env_vars.description: extra environment variables for the run

params.description: values asked for before the run

confirm.description: ask before every run, also when an agent starts it

history.description:
History is how many finished runs are kept on disk; 0 keeps only the
last run, in memory. Default 20.

about.description:
About shows the About tab: the folder's README.md, the environment den
sets and the parameters. Default true.

shell.description:
Shell is the command t opens in the runbook's folder, e.g.
"bash --rcfile .venv/bin/activate". Default $SHELL.

editor.description:
Editor is the command e opens the runbook's script with, and o a run's
log. Default $VISUAL, then $EDITOR, then vi.

agent.description:
Agent is the agent E changes the runbook with: a command line such as
`claude --model opus`, the name of a runbooks.agents entry, a kind such
as claude or opencode, or auto. Default runbooks.agent.

dirs.description:
Dirs are scanned for runbooks: every folder in them holding a
runbook.yaml is one, and so is an executable carrying a "# den:name"
header. Relative paths are read against den.yaml's directory.

rescan.description:
Rescan picks up runbook folders added, changed or removed while den
runs. On unless set to false.

template.description:
Template is a folder copied for a new runbook by `den runbook new` and
the Runbooks pane's n; empty uses the built-in one.

agent.description:
Agent is the agent that writes a runbook from a description (`den
runbook new --agent`, the pane's n): auto (the first agent CLI
installed, in the order agents' kind lists them), a kind such as claude
or opencode, or the name of an agents entry. Default auto, or the first
entry of agents when there are any.

agents.description:
Agents are command lines that write a runbook, for a model other than
the CLI's default or a wrapper such as `ollama launch opencode`. The
Runbooks pane's n offers them when there are two or more.

defaults.description:
Defaults apply to every runbook; a runbook.yaml or an items entry
overrides them one key at a time.

items.description: Items are runbooks declared inline, for the curated team-shared set.

sequences.description: runbooks run in order, stopping at the first failure

sources.description:
Sources are git repositories of runbook folders that den checks out
and lists beside your own, each runbook under its source's name:
platform-ops/rds-status. Nothing updates on its own: `den runbook
source update` moves a source to the newest commit of its ref.

allow_sources.description:
AllowSources limits the repositories a source may come from, as
host/owner/repo patterns with * wildcards: "ghe.acme.com/ops/*".
Empty allows any.

aws_profile.description: exported as AWS_PROFILE for KMS keys

auto_reveal.description: show every value in clear when the file opens

view.description: View is how secrets with nested values open, unless one sets its own.

SecretsConfig.description: SecretsConfig lists the secret sources shown in the Secrets pane, grouped by provider.

SequenceSpec.description: SequenceSpec runs named runbooks in order, stopping at the first failure.

type.description: which section below holds its settings

env.description: an entry of environments: its keys fill what the section leaves out

ServiceSpec.description: ServiceSpec describes one service entry in the config file.

host.description:
ssh: the destination (user@host) and extra ssh arguments such as
[-i, ~/.ssh/key, -J, jump.example.com]. Key or agent auth only: den
cannot answer a password prompt.

endpoint_id.description:
eice: the EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint ID. The service host is
resolved to an IP first, since the endpoint only tunnels to IPs.

resource.description:
kubectl: the resource to forward to (svc/x, deploy/x, pod/x), which
must itself serve the service's port — typically a proxy in front of
the database — plus an optional context and namespace.

context.description: kubectl: the kubeconfig context; the current one when empty

namespace.description: kubectl: the namespace; the context's when empty

TransportSpec.description: TransportSpec says how den reaches the network a service lives in.

vpn.description: name of an entry in the vpn: section

enabled.description:
Enabled switches the behaviour on (the default) or off, keeping the link
so den can still warn about a manual connect without the VPN.

TunnelAutoConnect.description: TunnelAutoConnect names the VPN a tunnel runs over.

reconnect.description: restart the tunnel after it drops, with backoff

health_check.description: host:port dialled through the command's -D SOCKS proxy to confirm the far side is reachable

monitor.description: re-run the connection checks every 15 s while connected; two misses count as a drop

auto_connect.description:
AutoConnect ties the tunnel to the VPN it runs over: den connects it once
that VPN is connected and stops it when the VPN goes down.

TunnelSpec.description: TunnelSpec describes one SSH tunnel entry in the config file.

github_api.description: releases/latest API URL of a fork or GitHub Enterprise server, e.g. https://api.github.com/repos/you/den/releases/latest; a fork on api.github.com reads its own release feed, and GITHUB_TOKEN, when set, makes den use the API

s3_bucket.description: an S3 mirror of the releases; wins over github_api

aws_profile.description: uses default AWS profile if omitted

UpdatesConfig.description: UpdatesConfig controls where den checks for and downloads new releases.

gateway.description: gateway host[:port]; required unless config_file is set

config_file.description: path to openfortivpn INI config file (-c flag)

health_check.description: host:port reachable ONLY via the VPN; probed to confirm the data path is alive

reconnect.description:
Reconnect re-establishes a tunnel that dropped after being fully connected.
Deliberately unlike tunnels: openfortivpn logs in through SAML, which opens a
browser tab, so retries are capped (see reconnectDelays) and a login that
times out is never retried — repeated half-finished logins burn the account's
FortiGate session slots until the gateway 403s every new login.

VPNSpec.description: VPNSpec describes one VPN entry in the config file.

path.description: secret path; a trailing "/" lists a folder

login.description: shell command run by L, e.g. vault login -method=oidc

auto_reveal.description: show every value in clear when opened

VaultSecretSpec.description: VaultSecretSpec is one HashiCorp Vault KV secret, or a folder of them when Path ends in "/", read with the vault CLI and the user's own token.

title.description: The dashboard's header line; "den — Developer Environment Navigator" when unset

aws.description: Where the AWS CLI files are and which SSO sessions to show

menu_order.description: panels to show, in this order; every panel when empty

environments.description: Named groups of shared bastion and profile settings; a service picks one with env:

services.description: The data stores and stacks the Connect panel lists

runbooks.description: Your scripts, run with den's connection context

logs.description: The log file and level of den itself

updates.description: Where den looks for new releases

mcp.description: What AI agents may do through den mcp
